newsitem.title: USA: Fingerhut says expense controls helped Q2.
newsitem.headline: Fingerhut says expense controls helped Q2.

text.p: Fingerhut Cos Inc said Thursday its results for the second quarter were bolstered by expense controls and lower delinquencies.

"We are delighted with our strong second quarter performance of both businesses," said Ted Deikel, Fingerhut's chairman and chief executive. "Our efforts to substantially improve the operating performance of our retail business and focus on strong revenue growth of Metris, our financial services subsidiary, were the key drivers during the quarter."
Earlier Fingerhut said it earned $9.9 million, or $0.20 a share, in the second quarter versus $2.1 million, or $0.04 a share, in the same period last year.

"The retail segment posted a $0.10 improvement in earnings per share, reflecting our focus on controlling expenses and reducing delinquency, which will allow us to free up cash to reinvest in growing the business," Deikel said in a statement.
"In addition, Metris continues to strengthen and diversify its revenue stream through strategic alliances, such as the card registration agreement reached with a new third party during the quarter."

Metris, which is Fingerhut's 83-percent owned financial services subsidiary, posted net income including minority interest of $8.1 million. Its impact on consolidated earnings was $0.16 in the second quarter, up from $5.0 million, or $0.10 a share, for the second quarter of 1996.

Metris' managed credit card loan portfolio increased 17 percent, or $308 million, during the second quarter bringing the portfolio to $2.1 billion at June 30. Also during the quarter, Metris generated about 188,000 new customers to end the quarter with nearly 1.6 million credit card accounts.

"We are beginning to reap the benefits of our efforts to increase profitability and reduce risk," said Peter Michielutti, executive vice president and chief operating officer. "We've tightened our credit granting criteria and accelerated our collection activities, which has reduced delinquencies during the quarter."
